critique: The render now reads convincingly as a full-frame snowy field: bright white flakes cover the frame, size variation is present, and the t1-to-t4 progression shows ongoing falling/emission. The principal remaining mismatch is temporal balance: t1 is visibly lighter than t4, while the thumbnail-like preset should feel established from the opening frame. Flakes are still biased toward fine, crisp dots; a somewhat larger soft foreground component would make the snow feel more layered and atmospheric.

suggestions.why: Shortening particle life reduces the excessive accumulation visible by t4, bringing its density closer to the already-established-looking t1 field.
A moderate emission increase restores early-frame coverage after reducing lifetime, so t1 feels populated without allowing t4 to become overwhelmingly dense.
Increasing maximum particle size adds a clearer foreground layer of larger soft flakes while retaining the fine background particles from size randomness.
